# Large files

Data files that are worth keeping with the repository but are too large for ordinary
Git — the shipped simulated alignment is 4 MB, a real alignment is hundreds — are
handled with [Git Large File Storage](https://git-lfs.com). Git LFS stores a small
pointer in the repository and the content on a separate server, so clones stay small.

## Install

```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
conda install -c conda-forge git git-lfs
git lfs install
```

`git-lfs` is part of the default pixi environment of this repository, so
`pixi run git lfs …` works without a separate installation.

## Configure

Track a file pattern, then commit the resulting `.gitattributes`:

```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
git lfs track "*.h5"
git add .gitattributes
git commit -m 'Added LFS'
git push
```

From then on every `.h5` file added to the repository goes to LFS instead of into the
Git object store. Patterns worth tracking in a pipeline repository are the ones that
grow without bound — `*.h5`, `*.maf`, `*.vcf.gz` — rather than everything under
`data/`.

::: { .callout-note }

Tracking applies to files added *after* the pattern is registered. Files already
committed stay in Git history, and moving them into LFS retroactively means rewriting
history.

:::

## Managing files

::: { .callout-warning }

Managing the LFS storage of a shared repository — quotas, purging old objects,
archives — is for the repository owner. See the GitHub documentation on
[configuring Git LFS](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/working-with-files/managing-large-files/configuring-git-large-file-storage)
and on
[LFS objects in archives](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/managing-your-repositorys-settings-and-features/managing-repository-settings/managing-git-lfs-objects-in-archives-of-your-repository).

:::

## What this repository does instead

Nothing here is currently in LFS. Two mechanisms keep the repository small without
it:

- The example alignment is *generated*, not stored at full size:
  `pixi run simulate-example` reproduces `data/simulated_alignment.maf` from a seeded
  msprime simulation.
- The published great-ape alignment is downloaded on demand with
  `pixi run download-example` and is listed in `.gitignore`.

Workflow output under `steps/` is ignored as well, since it is reproducible from the
input and the configuration.
